facts.statement: Julius von Haast first scientifically described the species in 1871 based on remains found by Frederick Richardson Fuller.
facts.quote: Haast's eagle was first scientifically described by Julius von Haast in 1871 from remains discovered by the Canterbury Museum taxidermist, Frederick Richardson Fuller, in a former marsh.

facts.statement: Fossils of the species date from the Pleistocene to the Late Holocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Pleistocene to Late Holocene

facts.statement: Females were larger than males, with estimated weights ranging from 10 to 18 kg for females and 9 to 12 kg for males.
facts.quote: Female eagles were larger than males. Most estimates place the female Haast's eagles in the range of 10–18 kg and males around 9 - 12 kg.

facts.statement: The wingspan of a grown female is estimated to have been up to 2.6 meters, possibly reaching 3 meters in some cases.
facts.quote: It is estimated that the grown female typically spanned up to 2.6 m, possibly up to 3 m in a few cases.

facts.statement: Its front-left talon measured between 4.9 and 6.15 cm, while the hallux-claw could reach up to 11 cm.
facts.quote: The talons of Haast's eagle were similar in length to those of the harpy eagle, with a front-left talon length of 4.9 to 6.15 cm and a hallux-claw of possibly up to 11 cm.

facts.statement: Its massive size evolved as a response to its primary prey, the flightless moa, which could weigh up to 200 kg.
facts.quote: Its massive size is explained as an evolutionary response to the size of its primary prey—the flightless moa—the largest of which could weigh 200 kg.

facts.statement: Despite its short wingspan, evidence strongly suggests the bird was capable of flight.
facts.quote: Haast's eagle's relatively short wingspan has sometimes led to it being incorrectly portrayed as having evolved toward flightlessness, even though evidence strongly suggests that it flew.

facts.statement: The eagle predominantly preyed on large, flightless birds, including the moa.
facts.quote: Haast's eagle predominantly preyed on large, flightless bird species, including the moa.

facts.statement: A 2021 analysis indicated that the bill was functionally closer to that of the Andean condor than to other eagles.
facts.quote: A 2021 analysis showed that, while predatory, the bill of Haast's eagle was functionally closer to that of the Andean condor (Vultur gryphus) than to that of other eagles.

facts.statement: Māori cave art found near Timaru depicts the eagle with a pale head.
facts.quote: Māori cave art depicts Haast's eagle with a pale head. These Māori rock art drawings can still be found in modern-day South Canterbury near Timaru.

facts.statement: Haast's eagles occupied the ecological niche of top mammalian predators in New Zealand.
facts.quote: Haast's eagles were the hunters who filled the same niche as top-niche mammalian predators.

facts.statement: Haast's eagles likely competed with Māori for food, and the eagle became extinct around the same time as its prey, the moa, which went extinct between 1440 and 1445.
facts.quote: The added hunting pressure from the Māori led the moa to extinction by around 1440 to 1445. Both eagles and Māori likely competed for the same foods.

facts.statement: Māori legends described the bird as huge with black-and-white plumage, yellow-green tinged wings, and a red crest.
facts.quote: According to an account given to George Grey, an early governor of New Zealand, Hōkioi were huge black-and-white birds with yellow-green tinged wings and a red crest.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Māori legends refer to Haast's eagle or to the extinct South Island Austral snipe.
facts.quote: However, it has also been argued that the "hakawai" and "hōkioi" legends refer to the Austral snipe—in particular the extinct South Island species.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest the pouākai legend does not refer to Haast's eagle because the species is not known to have lived on the North Island.
facts.quote: Additionally, it has been suggested that the pouākai is unlikely to refer to Haast's eagle as the species is not known to have been present at North Island.

facts.statement: The eagle was originally described by Julius von Haast in the 1870s from remains discovered by Frederick Richardson Fuller in an old swamp.
facts.quote: El águila de Haast fue descrita originalmente por Julius von Haast en la década de 1870, a partir de restos descubiertos por el taxidermista del Museo Canterbury, Frederick Richardson Fuller, en un antiguo pantano.

facts.statement: The species was named Harpagornis moorei in honor of George Henry Moore, who owned the Glenmark Estate where the bones were found.
facts.quote: Haast nombró al águila Harpagornis moorei en honor de George Henry Moore, el propietario de Glenmark Estate en donde se encontraron los huesos del ave.

facts.statement: DNA analysis in 2005 showed the eagle was closely related to the smaller Australian and shrike-hawk species of the genus Hieraaetus, not the larger booted eagle as previously thought.
facts.quote: Los análisis de ADN en 2005 han mostrado que esta rapaz estaba cercanamente relacionada con la mucho menor aguililla australiana, así como la aguililla calzada (ambas especies pertenecientes al género Hieraaetus) y no, como se pensó en principio, a la relativamente grande águila audaz.

facts.statement: Consequently, Harpagornis moorei was renamed Hieraaetus moorei.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, Harpagornis moorei fue renombrada como Hieraaetus moorei.

facts.statement: H. moorei may have diverged from these smaller hawks in a relatively recent period between 700,000 and 1.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: H. moorei puede haber divergido de estas aguilillas en un período relativamente reciente, comprendido entre 700 000 a 1.8 millones de años.

facts.statement: The eagle's massive size increase was possible partly due to the presence of large prey and the absence of competition from other large predators.
facts.quote: Esto fue posible en parte gracias a la presencia de grandes presas y a la ausencia de competencia de otros grandes depredadores.

facts.statement: A later mitochondrial DNA study determined it was more closely related to the Australian goshawk than the shrike-hawk, with an evolutionary divergence from the Australian goshawk estimated at nearly 2.2 million years.
facts.quote: Un estudio posterior de ADN mitocondrial determinó que se relacionaba más cercanamente con la aguililla australiana que con la aguililla calzada, con una divergencia evolutiva de la aguililla australiana estimada en cerca de 2.2 millones de años.

facts.statement: The eagle went extinct around 1400 AD when its main food source, the moa, was hunted to extinction by Māori and its dense forest habitat was largely devastated.
facts.quote: El águila de Haast se extinguió hacia el año 1400 d. C., cuando su principal fuente alimenticia, los moas, fueron cazados hasta la extinción por los maoríes y la mayor parte de su hábitat de bosques densos fue devastado.

facts.statement: It was the largest eagle known to science.
facts.quote: Fue el águila de mayor tamaño que se conoce.

facts.statement: Its main prey were moa, giant flightless birds unable to defend themselves against the impact force and speed of these eagles, which could reach speeds of 80 km/h.
facts.quote: Su presa principal eran moas, aves gigantes no voladoras e incapaces de defenderse de la fuerza de choque y la velocidad de estas águilas, las cuales podían alcanzar una velocidad de 80 km/h.

facts.statement: The eagle's large size may have been an evolutionary response to its prey size, as it would have been substantially smaller when it arrived on the island before growing substantially over time due to a lack of competition (see island gigantism).
facts.quote: El gran tamaño del águila puede haber sido una respuesta evolutiva al tamaño de sus presas, ya que habría sido sustancialmente menor cuando arribó a la isla, para luego crecer sustancialmente a lo largo del tiempo debido a la carencia de competencia (véase gigantismo insular).

facts.statement: The fossil range of the species spans the Pleistocene to the Holocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Pleistoceno-Holoceno

facts.statement: The species is estimated to have gone extinct around 1400.
facts.quote: extinct: c. 1400

facts.statement: The species authority is listed as Haast, 1872.
facts.quote: species_authority: (Haast, 1872)

facts.statement: The Haast eagle was the largest known bird of prey, slightly larger than the largest vultures.
facts.quote: Las águilas de Haast fueron las mayores rapaces conocidas, levemente mayores incluso que los más grandes buitres

facts.statement: Estimates place female Haast eagles at 10 to 15 kg and males at around 9 to 12 kg.
facts.quote: Muchas estimaciones sitúan a las águilas de Haast hembras en el rango de 10 a 15 kg y a los machos en alrededor de 9 a 12 kg

facts.statement: One source estimated that the largest females could have weighed more than 16.5 kg.
facts.quote: Una fuente estimó que las mayores hembras pudieron haber llegado a pesar más de 16.5 kg de masa

facts.statement: They had a relatively short wingspan for their size, measuring approximately 2.6 to over 3 meters in some cases.
facts.quote: Tenían una envergadura relativamente corta para su tamaño, midiendo aproximadamente 2.6 hasta más de 3 m en algunos casos

facts.statement: A lower jaw of the Haast eagle measured 11.4 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Una mandíbula inferior del águila de Haast medía 11,4 centímetros de largo

facts.statement: The tarsus in several fossils has been measured between 22.7 and 24.9 centimeters.
facts.quote: el tarso en varios fósiles ha sido medido entre 22,7 a 24,9 centímetros

facts.statement: The talons were similar in length to the harpy eagle, with a front-left claw measuring 4.9 to 6.15 cm and a hallux claw of possibly more than 11 cm.
facts.quote: Las garras del águila de Haast eran similares en longitud a las del águila harpía, con una longitud frontal-izquierda de 4,9 a 6,15 centímetros y una garra del hallux de posiblemente más de 11 centímetros

facts.statement: The tail was certainly very long, over 50 centimeters in female specimens, and very wide.
facts.quote: La cola era seguramente muy larga, de más de 50 centímetros en los especímenes hembra, y muy ancha

facts.statement: The total body length is estimated at over 1.4 meters in females, with a standing height of approximately 90 centimeters or slightly more.
facts.quote: Se estima la longitud corporal total en más de 1,4 metros en la hembras, con una altura en posición erguida de aproximadamente 90 centímetros o quizás levemente mayor

facts.statement: It is estimated that it attacked at speeds of more than 80 kilometers per hour.
facts.quote: Se estima que atacaba a velocidades de más de 80 kilómetros por hora

facts.statement: Its size and weight indicate that it exerted a striking force equivalent to a block of cement falling from the top of an eight-story building.
facts.quote: Su tamaño y peso indican que ejercía una fuerza corporal de golpe equivalente al de un bloque de cemento que cae desde lo alto de un edificio de ocho pisos

facts.statement: Haast eagles preyed on large flightless bird species, including moas.
facts.quote: Las águilas de Haast depredaban a las grandes especies de aves no voladoras, incluyendo a las moas

facts.statement: It frequently grabbed the prey's pelvis with one foot and killed it with a blow to the head or neck with the other foot.
facts.quote: con frecuencia aferrándose a la pelvis de la presa con las garras de un pie y matándola con un golpe a la cabeza o el cuello con el otro pie

facts.statement: Its large beak may also have been used to tear the internal organs of its prey, causing death by blood loss.
facts.quote: Su gran pico también pudo haber sido usado para rasgar los órganos internos de su presa, causándole la muerte por pérdida de sangre

facts.statement: The first human settlers in New Zealand, the Maori who arrived around the year 1280, hunted intensively local large flightless birds, including all moa species, leading to their eventual extinction.
facts.quote: Los primeros pobladores humanos en Nueva Zelanda, los maoríes que arribaron alrededor del año 1280, cazaron intensivamente a las grandes aves no voladoras locales, incluyendo a todas las especies de moas, conduciéndolas finalmente a su extinción

facts.statement: The loss of its natural prey caused the Haast eagle to also go extinct by the year 1400.
facts.quote: La pérdida de sus presas naturales causó que igualmente el águila de Haast se extinguiera por el año 1400

facts.statement: Charles Edward Douglas claimed in his diaries that he encountered two enormous raptors in the Landsborough River valley (probably during the 1870s) and shot and ate them.
facts.quote: Charles Edward Douglas, afirmó en sus diarios que él tuvo un encuentro con dos rapaces de enorme tamaño en el valle del Río Landsborough (probablemente durante la década de 1870), y que él les disparó y se alimentó con estas

facts.statement: Some argue that there could not have been appropriate prey to sustain a Haast eagle population for nearly five hundred years prior to this record.
facts.quote: algunos sostienen que no podía haber presas apropiadas como para sostener una población de águilas de Haast por cerca de quinientos años anteriores a la fecha de este registro

facts.statement: A more probable explanation, considering the supposed three-meter wingspan given by Douglas is surely only a rough estimate, is that the birds in question were Eyles' harriers.
facts.quote: una explicación más probable, tomando en cuenta que la supuesta envergadura de tres metros dada por Douglas es seguramente solo una estimación burda, es que las aves en cuestión fueran aguiluchos de Eyles

facts.statement: Its parent group is Accipitridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Accipitridae

facts.statement: Its family is Accipitridae.
facts.quote: Family: Accipitridae

facts.statement: Its time range is the Late Pleistocene to Holocene (0.129 to 0 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Late Pleistocene to Holocene (0.129 to 0 million years ago)

facts.statement: Eight fossil occurrences have been recorded.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 8
